Prevention: Plant certified seeds and disease-free transplants
Use correct plant spacing i.e. 60cm x 60cm (outdoor) and 60cm x 45cm (greenhouse) for proper aeration
Irrigate early in the morning to allow the leaves to dry
Rotate tomatoes with non- solanaceous crops e.g. maize or beans
Monitoring: Dark brown to black lesions of various sizes and shapes on leaves, fruit and stems, initially surrounded by a yellow halo and concentrated near leaf margins
Small slightly raised dark brown to black tiny flecks in immature fruit.
Raised black spots on mature fruit that are superficial, rarely penetrating deep and can be scraped by a fingernail
Stunted growth with delayed fruit maturity.
Take action when specks are seen on 1 plant
Direct Control: Disinfect all farm tools in 10% jik solution (50mls in 1 litre of water) for 5 minutes
Start working from the healthy field towards the infected
Restrictions: Bacterial diseases have no known cure hence avoid the introducing the pathogen.
Use of copper-based fungicides only suppresses the pathogen.
When using a pesticide always wear protective equipment.

Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
